speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of delivering an 11-pound baby and the specific report of decreased bowel sounds with uterine tenderness raises concern for a uterine infection or potential abdominal complication. Given the risk of obstetric infection, have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and did you experience any chills or rigors recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Blood Cultures
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and urine culture
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text:
I see your results are still pending, but the report of decreased bowel sounds alongside uterine tenderness is very concerning for postpartum endometritis or a pelvic abscess. Have you noticed any changes in your vaginal discharge, such as a foul odor, or have you developed rigors?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Pending results aside, your report of decreased bowel sounds alongside uterine tenderness is highly concerning for a uterine infection extending into the abdomen or a pelvic abscess. Has your abdominal pain become more severe since delivery, and are you currently able to pass gas or have a bowel movement?
